text:
[title] PagedAttention + speculative decoding: 2.4x goodput at p99
[body] KV-cache fragmentation: <4% waste via block tables
[body] Draft model acceptance alpha = 0.78 at gamma = 5
[body] Continuous batching; chunked prefill off to hold the TTFT SLO

novice.takeaway: The slide claims combining two technical methods (PagedAttention and speculative decoding) boosts serving performance 2.4x while managing memory waste and response-time targets.
questions: What is speculative decoding and how does it help?
What does 'TTFT SLO' mean in practice?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe their technical optimizations significantly improve serving speed and efficiency.

peer.takeaway: Combining memory-efficient caching (PagedAttention) with speculative decoding and batching techniques yields a 2.4x improvement in p99 goodput for LLM serving.
questions: What is 'gamma' controlling in speculative decoding?
How does chunked prefill affect latency tradeoffs?
What baseline is the 2.4x goodput compared against?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their combined technique substantially improves LLM serving efficiency and latency.

expert.takeaway: Combining PagedAttention with speculative decoding (draft acceptance rate 0.78 at gamma=5) plus tuned batching/prefill config yields the claimed 2.4x p99 goodput gain.
questions: Why is chunked prefill disabled specifically?
What baseline is the 2.4x goodput measured against?
What is the draft model architecture/size used?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to accept these specific optimizations as the source of the 2.4x p99 goodput gain.
